Theorem
[Maximum principle for the Cauchy problem, small-time case]

↗ lem:comparison-function-solves-heat ↗ thm:weak-maximum-principle-heat \group Maximum Principles

Let $u\in C(\R ^n\times [0,T])$ be $C^2$ and solve the heat equation on $\R ^n\times (0,T)$. Suppose $u(x,0)\le M$, $u(x,t)\le Ae^{a|x|^2}$, and $4aT<1$. Then \[ u\le M\quad \text{on }\R ^n\times [0,T]. \]
Proof

\sketch Choose $\varepsilon >0$ with $4a(T+\varepsilon )<1$, compare $u$ with $\mu K$ on $B(y,r)\times (0,T]$, and apply the weak maximum principle. The initial boundary is bounded by $M$, while the backward Gaussian dominates the growth term on the lateral boundary as $r\to \infty $. Let $\mu \downarrow 0$.

□
